title: Embedding quantization strategy: INT8 weights + FP16 activations and cosine-drift validation
creator: Ana Patel
description: Goal: define and validate a production-ready quantization profile for production embedding models that uses INT8 weight quantization combined with FP16 activation execution, and establish an automated cosine-similarity drift validation workflow. Deliverables: (1) quantization profile spec (per-tensor vs per-channel, symmetric/asymmetric, clip rules, outlier handling), (2) calibration pipeline and datasets, (3) evaluation harness for cosine similarity + retrieval metrics, (4) rollout plan with rollback gates and telemetry dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Quantization profile doc reviewed and merged (per-channel INT8 for weights; FP16 path for activations)
Calibration pipeline produces calibration tables and quant params reproducibly for given corpora
Mean cosine similarity to FP32 baseline >= 0.995 on eval set and median drop <= 0.5%
Recall@10 degradation <= 1% on retrieval bench for customer-like workloads
Automated validation job (CI) that runs on each candidate build and emits pass/fail
Rollout runbook and telemetry alerts defined for mean_cosine_drop, p95_latency, and error-rate
work_items: WIP: capture representative calibration corpora (public + internal prod traces anonymized)
Implement per-channel symmetric INT8 weight quantizer with support for outlier clipping (configurable clip percentile)
FP16 activation execution path integration in runtime (ensure KV cache FP16 compatibility)
Calibration tooling: collect min/max/scale or histogram-based moments per-layer and persist tables
Evaluation harness: compute pairwise cosine similarity to FP32 baseline, compute recall@k/ndcg, and sample drift distributions
Create CI job that runs quantization + eval for PRs against embedding models (timeout ~2h, parallel shards)
Dashboard: mean_cosine_diff, recall_drop, traffic% for canary, and automatic rollback triggers
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Chose per-channel INT8 for weights because it reduces representational error for dense linear layers compared to per-tensor and yields smaller cosine drift in prior experiments
Keep activations in FP16: avoids dynamic range clipping complexities and preserves runtime stability for KV cache / autoregressive code paths
Use symmetric quantization for weights as default (zero-point = 0) because embeddings are centered and symmetric scales simplified inference kernels; asymmetric kept as opt-in for specific ops
Calibration method: prefer histogram-based percentile clipping over naive min/max to reduce sensitivity to outliers; tradeoff is additional memory/compute during calibration
Avoid full QAT (quantization-aware training) as first pass due to cost/time; plan QAT as follow-up for models that fail threshold
calibration_workflow: Step 1: Select calibration corpus: 100k representative sentences including short/long tails and domain-specific subsets
Step 2: Run forward-pass collection with FP32 model to gather per-tensor activation histograms and weight ranges
Step 3: Derive scales using 99.9th percentile clipping by default; provide flags for 99.5/99.99 for sensitivity tests
Step 4: Emit calibration tables with deterministic format and checksum, store in artifact storage (s3://redwood-quant-calib/<model>/<commit>)
Step 5: Apply quant params to model weights (per-channel INT8) and materialize quantized artifact; runtime will route activations through FP16 compute kernels
Step 6: Run evaluation harness against held-out eval set and production-like retrieval tasks; produce metrics and artifacts
evaluation_metrics_and_thresholds: Mean cosine similarity to FP32 baseline: >= 0.995 (primary metric)
Recall@1 / Recall@10 degradation: <= 1% relative to FP32
Cosine distribution tail checks: fraction of pairs with similarity < 0.8 should not increase by more than 0.2%
Throughput improvement: expected 1.6x-2.2x speedup for weight-load bound kernels on GPU with INT8 weights + FP16 activations
Latency p95 change: <= +5ms relative to current FP16 baseline (hard guard)
Model size reduction: weight memory savings ~2x compared to FP16 baseline
benchmarks_and_results: Initial microbenchmarks (internal, 2026-03-10) on text-embed-4-small: mean_cosine = 0.9961, median_drop = 0.28%, recall@10 drop = 0.6%
KV cache sanity: no observed corruption when activations run in FP16 and weights are INT8 in synthetic trace test
Throughput test on A100-80GB: 1.9x token/sec improvement for embedding forward pass when using INT8 weights
Edge case: outlier-heavy biology dataset showed mean cosine 0.992 -> added 99.99th percentile calibration option
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: calibration corpus not representative —> Mitigation: include automated sampling from production (anonymized) and maintain per-customer test slices
Risk: rare precision regressions for certain queries —> Mitigation: implement per-request fallback to FP16/FP32 if validation probe sample falls below threshold
Risk: quantized artifacts incompatible with older runtime kernels —> Mitigation: add artifact manifest with runtime-min-version and compatibility checks in deploy pipeline
Risk: evaluation benchmark doesn't reflect real retrieval downstream —> Mitigation: run AB tests on 1% traffic with canary and monitor downstream KPIs
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal QA on staging cluster with synthetic traffic (0% prod traffic)
Stage 1: canary with 1% of production traffic and extended evaluation (24-72h), automated monitor for mean_cosine_drop > 0.002 triggers rollback
Stage 2: ramp to 10% for 48h if no alerts, compare downstream product metrics (search CTR, rerank quality)
Stage 3: full rollout with weekly checks for the first month
Rollback criteria: mean_cosine_drop > 0.002, recall@10 drop > 1.5%, or p95 latency increase > 10%
implementation_notes: CI job: quant-eval (runs nightly and on PRs); see .github/workflows/quant-eval.yml
Runtime change: kernel flag --enable-int8-weights --activation-fp16 required; default off until GA
